sources_considered.why: An original investigation documents substantial reach for apparent AI-generated conspiracy content before the post.
Primary research documents AI spam and recommendations, but its expanded sample extends beyond the post and its explanation of the algorithm is explicitly tentative.
Platform documentation supplies a competing account of recommendation design, although it is older and not an independent performance audit.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph describing the fictional explorer Tommy Brady

receipt.public_excerpt: This video garnered over 1.9 million views.

evidence_items.explanation: The investigation observed substantial reach for a video apparently using AI-generated imagery. This supports successful examples, but supplies no matched comparison establishing that volume outweighed quality or caused the reach.

evidence_items.locator: Essay Summary, paragraph on Facebook Feed recommendations
evidence_items.explanation: The study documents recommendations of AI imagery but identifies the engagement mechanism as a suspicion. Its expanded sample and observations extend beyond the post, so it is contextual rather than decisive evidence of the contemporaneous claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: We also don't recommend duplicated content

evidence_items.explanation: TikTok describes safeguards against repetition and spam. This challenges a simple account of design that rewards volume, but stated safeguards do not establish their effectiveness in March 2024.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved comparison separates the effect of production volume from audience preferences, content characteristics and account history.
The evidence does not establish that platforms reward volume over quality far more often, or verify a general earnings advantage.
